title: R4-v2: T22 feasibility with separated development/evaluation designs and a fail-closed R1 gate

supersedes.what_changes: the single feasibility part is split into (a) evaluation-file power/coverage at a fixed development design and (b) development-data adequacy at a fixed evaluation design; the exact bound P(supported) <= 1 - P(withheld) screens infeasible designs before any large-file production

r4_protocol_v1.what_is_retained: the eval-file grid, development grid, feasibility rules and controls
r4_protocol_v1.what_changes: separate development n_cal from evaluation n_cal; full-scenario development table keys; include the any-null-family error and completeness in the feasibility decision; apply the frozen accepted R1 candidate; fail-closed R1 gate enforced at the run boundary

provenance.observed_before_design: the September T22-S feasibility failure at 4/8/16 files, the withholding of 0.94-0.96 and the medium-effect power of 0.02-0.04 were observed before this protocol was written
provenance.source_change_recorded: R4 uses explicit separate development and evaluation random streams (streams.py); the archived simulator is single-stream and is not edited

question: Which evaluation-file counts and development-data conditions jointly meet the original feasibility requirements (primary coverage in tolerance, type-I control, worst-case non-drift withholding <= 0.5, medium-effect unconditional power >= 0.5, at least four independent files), and does the development gate make the criterion unreachable regardless of evaluation-file count?

hypotheses.H1_eval_module: descriptive: at a fixed development design, evaluation coverage, type-I, withholding, unconditional and conditional medium-effect power are reported at n_files = 4/8/16/32/64
hypotheses.H2_dev_module: descriptive: at a fixed evaluation design (n_files = 16), the withholding rate and primary coverage are reported over a development grid n_dev_files in {4,8,16} x n_cal in {64,256}
hypotheses.H3_bound: the exact bound P(supported) <= 1 - P(withheld) is computed with Wilson uncertainty; a design whose withholding cannot fall below 0.5 is screened infeasible and is not extended
hypotheses.H4_feasibility: the original feasibility rule is applied unchanged; the correct output may be a feasibility failure
hypotheses.H5_streams: changing n_files must not change the development realization, and changing the development design must not change the evaluation realization (separate streams)

independent_unit: one simulated collection of files (one Monte-Carlo replicate); evaluation and development data are drawn from separate declared streams

estimands.primary: the equal-file mean of the per-file population contrasts (unchanged from T22-S)
estimands.power: P('supported' | alternative) unconditionally and given not withheld; unconditional power is capped by 1 - withholding
estimands.withholding: P(dependence verdict inconclusive), a property of the development files and the frozen maximum rule

streams_are_separate.checks: changing n_files leaves the development realization identical

support_bound_arithmetic.checks: P(supported) <= 1 - P(withheld) on a fixed synthetic record set

estimand_identity.checks: 10 small replicates are invariant-clean and their mean bias is small

inference.coverage_rule: Wilson interval not entirely outside the band

feasibility.rule: a matched instrument comparison is feasible at n available independent files only if n >= 4, the confirmation calibration is complete and within tolerance at the largest calibrated n_files <= n, the maximum withholding over non-drift scenarios at that n_files is <= 0.5, the medium-effect unconditional power is >= 0.5, and the development-data dependence verdict is not inconclusive
feasibility.screening: unconditional support probability cannot exceed 1 - withholding; screen infeasible designs with the Wilson bound before pricing large-file counts

r1_precondition.rule: R4's large-file production cells (n_files = 32 and 64) are admissible only if R1 yields a usable interval. The precondition FAILS (cancel, not defer) if: R1's frozen primary replacement is 'none'; OR R1's acceptance receipt shows a coverage or type-I failure at any candidate file count; OR the withholding-bound screen rules out every candidate design. It is UNRESOLVED while R1 has not frozen an interval and acceptance receipt, and PASSES only when a frozen, accepted candidate exists and the screen is not universal.
r1_precondition.on_cancel: emit an R4_INFEASIBLE receipt naming the trigger, omit the cancelled cells from the matrix, launch plan and cost report, and do NOT stage them as ready to transfer

inference.design_separation: development n_cal and n_dev_files are separate parameters from the evaluation design; the evaluation calibration length is fixed at CAL_EVAL=64
inference.inference_source: the frozen accepted R1 candidate from the R1-to-R4 gate; the archived baseline is retained as a labelled comparison

stopping_rule: fixed allocation: production is 20 chunks per scenario x (16 evaluation-grid scenarios + 12 development-grid scenarios) x 50 MC = 28,000 replicates; the n_files=32/64 evaluation cells are CANCELLED and omitted before execution when the R1 precondition fails; infeasible n_files screened out by H3 are also removed from the launch plan

failure_interpretation.feasibility_failure: the correct output of the rule; reported with its reasons and never converted into an artificial four-file significance claim
failure_interpretation.screened_infeasible: the development gate makes the power requirement unreachable; report it and omit unnecessary large-file production
failure_interpretation.gate_change_required: a gate candidate or a development-dimension change requires a new protocol version with full type-I/coverage validation and fresh confirmation; it is never forced in a scientific run
failure_interpretation.conditional_power_only: conditional-on-not-withheld power is not a substitute for unconditional power

budget.retry_policy: failed cells are charged and retried only by an explicit --allow-repeat

explicitly_not_claimed: that increasing evaluation files alone can lower withholding; the gate is computed from development files
that the synthetic dependence model is the instrument's dependence structure
any adequacy of the archived inference on unexamined instrument data
any change to the archived T22 verdicts (all withheld)
any scientific result from fixture (development) runs
that the R1 cancellation gate can be bypassed to run large-file cells when R1 froze 'none' or failed; a cancel is final for this protocol version

change_log.change: initial R4 protocol (superseded by v2; retained)
separated dev/eval designs; dev-table scenario identity; any-null-family + completeness in feasibility; frozen R1 inference applied; fail-closed gate at the run boundary
